title: Samson, Dhir Power India to Record 226 Chase Against New Zealand
excerpt: Sanju Samson made 67 off 33 balls and Naman Dhir finished unbeaten on 42 off 15 as India reached 230 for 6 in 19.4 overs in Christchurch, beating New Zealand by four wickets in the first T20I.
body:
• India chased 226 to beat New Zealand by four wickets in Christchurch, their highest successful chase in T20 internationals, reaching 230 for 6 in 19.4 overs.
  • Sanju Samson set the pace with 67 off 33 balls, including eight fours and four sixes, after a 93-run opening stand with Abhishek Sharma.
  • Glenn Phillips made an unbeaten 82 off 40 balls for New Zealand, whose 225 for 4 was not enough despite a middle-overs fightback by their spinners.
  • India lead the five-match series 1-0, with the second T20I also at Hagley Oval on Saturday.

India completed their highest successful chase in T20 internationals on Thursday, hunting down 226 to beat New Zealand by four wickets in the first match of a five-game series at Hagley Oval in Christchurch. According to IANS, Sanju Samson hammered 67 off 33 balls and Naman Dhir finished the chase with an unbeaten 42 off 15 balls, taking India to 230 for 6 with two balls to spare in front of a sell-out crowd.

The previous mark listed by the Times of India was 209, achieved against Australia in Visakhapatnam in 2023 and against New Zealand in Raipur in 2026. The Christchurch chase moved well beyond that, in a match that produced 455 runs across the two innings.

"Matches can be finished in the first half. I think six overs, 90-odd runs, great start today."

— Sanju Samson, India batter

How the Chase Was Built

India raced to 94 for 1 in the powerplay. Samson and Abhishek Sharma put on 93 for the first wicket, attacking Matt Henry, Adam Milne and Lockie Ferguson from the start. Abhishek made 29 off 12 balls, launching the last delivery of the first over for six, while Samson reached fifty off 23 balls. According to IANS, Samson's six off Henry was India's 350th maximum in T20 internationals this year, the most by any team in a calendar year.

New Zealand then pulled the game back. Captain Mitchell Santner bowled Samson off an under-edge in the ninth over, after the opener had hit eight fours and four sixes. Michael Bracewell removed Abhishek and Tilak Varma, who made 6 off 11 balls, and Santner dismissed Ishan Kishan for 1. India slipped from 93 without loss to 122 for 4 in the 11th over, losing three wickets for seven runs in one phase described by the Times of India.

Captain Shreyas Iyer steadied the innings with 42 off 28 balls. Axar Patel added 24 off 14 balls before Ferguson dismissed him. Dhir then took over, hitting a six and a four when Santner returned, and, after Iyer fell at the start of the 19th over, he sealed the win in the final over, driving Henry for four and top-edging a short ball over the keeper for six, according to IANS.

Phillips Lifts New Zealand to 225

Earlier, India won the toss and bowled. New Zealand reached 65 for 1 in the powerplay and finished on 225 for 4 in 20 overs, according to the IANS brief scores. Finn Allen made 45 off 24 balls, Tim Seifert made 24 off 17, Daryl Mitchell made 28 and Bevon Jacobs made 31 off 16. Phillips was the standout, finishing unbeaten on 82 off 40 balls, his 13th T20I fifty, with strong running between the wickets noted by both IANS and AFP reporting carried by SA Cricket Mag.

None of India's bowlers conceded less than 10 runs an over. Axar Patel took 1 for 51, Bhuvneshwar Kumar conceded 49 without a wicket, Arshdeep Singh, playing his 100th T20I, took 1 for 45, and Mayank Yadav took 1 for 40. New Zealand scored 67 runs in the final five overs, setting a target that would usually be enough, particularly on a ground with long boundaries that had troubled India's middle order.

What It Means and What Comes Next

The result gives India a 1-0 lead in the five-match series and continues a run of high scoring that IANS said they carried from the West Indies series into New Zealand.

For New Zealand, the review will focus on the powerplay bowling and fielding. IANS noted 17 extras conceded and erratic lines early on, plus dropped chances for Mitchell, Iyer and Dhir. Santner and Bracewell, who took two wickets each, showed that spin through the middle overs could slow India, but the hosts could not stitch together tight overs at the start or the finish.

The second T20I will be played at the same venue, Hagley Oval, on Saturday. India will look to confirm that their opening pair and late-order hitting can repeat the approach, while New Zealand need a tighter powerplay plan if they are to defend or set a similar total in the next game.
